segments.caption: A beekeeper documents the installation of a vertical log hive, inoculated with propolis and beeswax, into a tree at a 10-foot height, complete with three entrance holes and an observation port. The segment concludes with the arrival of a swarm on April 4, 2013, which moves into the newly prepared hive.

The video shows a close-up of a large tree trunk with a freshly cut, circular opening, revealing the light-colored wood inside. A person’s hand points to the opening, which is secured with a patterned rope tied around the tree. Text on the screen identifies this as the “First opening,” taken six days after the tree was cut, on April 10, 2013. A person inspects a tree trunk where a circular wooden panel has been installed, secured with rope, and is being opened to reveal a small, dark hole inside the wood, with text indicating this is the "First opening" six days after an event on April 10, 2013.
A close-up view reveals a dense cluster of bees actively moving over a dark, textured surface inside a wooden structure, likely a hive or nest, with visible wood grain and a small hole nearby.

A person opens a tree cavity 17 days after the emergence of a brood, revealing a dense cluster of dark, newly hatched bees covered in white fungal growth, indicating an active, possibly diseased, bee colony.

The frames show a close-up view inside a wooden structure, likely a beehive or hollow log, where a large, dense cluster of bees is actively moving and clustering around a white, possibly wax or propolis, surface. The bees are tightly packed, indicating a high level of activity, possibly related to brood care, swarming, or hive maintenance. The scene is focused on the bees' persistent movement and interaction within their confined environment.

A bee swarm is shown clustered densely on a rope, then moves into a tree cavity. The scene progresses to show the tree with a new, larger opening, labeled "Third Opening" and dated May 11, 2013, 37 days after the swarm's arrival. The final frame shows a rope tied across a freshly cut circular opening in the tree trunk, indicating a human intervention to manage or access the hive.
A person uses a rope tied around a tree to pull open a hollowed-out section, revealing a dense swarm of bees inside the cavity.

A bee swarm, densely packed and covered in white, is shown clinging to the inside of a wooden structure. The scene then cuts to a hand securing a rope around a tree, with text indicating it is the "Forth opening" 11 weeks after "birth," dated June 22, 2013.

A person’s hand is shown interacting with a rope tied around a tree, which has a large, circular opening in its trunk. The hand first adjusts the rope, then points to the opening, and finally presses against the exposed wood inside. Text on the first frame indicates this is the “Forth opening,” 11 weeks after “birth,” dated June 22, 2013, suggesting the tree is part of an ongoing project or experiment.
A hand lifts a wooden lid from a hollow in a tree trunk, revealing a dense swarm of bees inside the cavity.

A beekeeper carefully removes a large, hollowed-out section of a tree trunk, revealing a dense swarm of bees clustered inside and on the cut surface, then holds it up for inspection before carefully lowering it back into place.

A close-up view reveals a large, rugged tree trunk with ropes securing it, leading to a hollow cavity where a thriving wild bee colony is nestled. The camera zooms into the cavity, showcasing dense clusters of bees actively moving over and around sections of honeycomb, indicating a bustling and healthy hive within the natural tree cavity.
A dense swarm of bees actively moves across and clings to honeycomb frames within a wooden hive, showcasing the hive’s bustling, living interior.
A hand gently probes a dense cluster of bees swarming over a honeycomb, revealing the hive's active interior and the bees' constant movement around the hexagonal cells.

The video opens with a close-up view of a bustling honeycomb, teeming with bees actively moving over the hexagonal cells. The scene then abruptly shifts to a dark, murky interior, possibly a cavity or a nest, where a single, faintly glowing object is visible. The video concludes with a transition to a textured, aged paper background, followed by a final black screen, suggesting an end or a pause in the narrative.
